findings.claim: The cleanups at :381 and :425 call getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) with the literal alias "alias". They never remove the created IDPs idp-alias-0..idp-alias-20, so each cleanup targets an IDP that does not exist.
findings.evidence: All four seats quote the same call. The pattern was copied from the pre-existing line 303. superpowers adds that create(idpRep).close() never checks the response status, so a duplicate-alias conflict would also go unnoticed. That only matters if the test realm is not re-imported between tests, which no seat checked.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats and undisputed. Fix: register cleanup against the alias each loop iteration actually creates. The identical bug at :303 predates the patch and goes to the ledger as non-blocking, out of the fix scope. Minor, so no red test is required.

verifier.reason: In OrganizationCacheTest.java:381, the loop creates the IDPs "idp-alias-" + i, and :424 creates "idp-alias-20". Both cleanups (:381, :425) register testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal "alias", so no cleanup ever removes the IDPs the test created. This copies the existing bug at :303.

findings.claim: An undocumented behaviour change to a public SPI predicate. The patch adds `organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` to LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), which is also the base filter in IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() (IdentityProviderBean.java:226). In that non-org-aware bean, an IDP the user has already linked is now hidden if it is bound to an organization and not BROKER_PUBLIC; before the patch it was shown. This goes beyond the commit title (cache for getForLogin), as does the isEnabled() re-filter at OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80.
findings.evidence: mattpocock cites CONTRIBUTING.md ("No changes to code not directly related to your PR") and PR-CHECKLIST.md, and traces the plain bean to FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:481-485. superpowers notes that IDPs are not wrapped when the Organization feature is off (Infinispan provider line 433), so an org-linked non-public IDP is now hidden there. ponytail raises the same point without investigating it. Counterpoint from open-code-review (checked, no finding): when a realm has organizations off, org-linked IDPs were already filtered out by the wrapper's isEnabled(), so it found no practical regression. ponytail says the clause is needed so that invalidation matches what the query returns. All reasoned; nothing was run.
findings.reason: Three seats raised it. open-code-review's counterpoint covers only realm-level org disablement, not the feature-off unwrapped path superpowers cites, so it does not disprove the claim. Keep the clause, since ponytail says invalidation needs it. Fix by documenting the behaviour change, or by scoping the predicate locally to the Infinispan provider as mattpocock suggests. Whether the change is intended is unverified: issue #32573 was never fetched.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` to LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254), which the plain bean uses at IdentityProviderBean.java:226 when organizations are off (FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:482-485). With the Organization feature disabled, IDPs are not wrapped (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:433), so a linked org-bound non-public IDP that showed before is now hidden; with the feature on, the wrapper's isEnabled() (line 441) or the org-aware predicate (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:94) already hid it, so the change is narrow.

findings.claim: The login cache goes stale when an org-linked IDP is edited while its organization is disabled. update() takes `original` from getById() (line 91), which is the org-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false while the org is disabled. `updated` is a plain model. If the edit sets hideOnLogin, sets linkOnly or removes BROKER_PUBLIC, the predicate fails for both models and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early (lines 403-407) without invalidating. When the org is re-enabled, the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL ID lists still contain the IDP. The cached path (lines 244-252) resolves it, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (:75,:80) re-checks only isEnabled(), so the hidden, link-only or private IDP is rendered on the login page.
findings.evidence: Both correctness seats independently trace the same sequence. The wrapper is createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (lines 430-445). The plain update model comes from IdentityProviderResource.updateIdpFromRep → RepresentationToModel.toModel (line 191). Org re-enable does not touch the login keys (InfinispanOrganizationProvider.registerOrganizationInvalidation, ~300-310). The proposed repro (not run): populate the ORG_ONLY cache, disable the org, set hideOnLogin=true or remove BROKER_PUBLIC on an org IDP, then assert that cacheKeyForLogin(realm, ORG_ONLY) is null (it is non-null on the patched code). Then re-enable the org and assert that getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, …) excludes the IDP (it does not on the patched code). Proposed fix: evaluate the predicate on the unwrapped stored model (idpDelegate.getById), as remove() already does with idpDelegate.getByAlias. superpowers #5 notes the new test has no disabled-org coverage, which is exactly where this bug sits.
findings.reason: Two seats, so it falls below the three-seat threshold and goes to the appendix: not reported as a review comment and not fixed this loop. No report contradicts it. ponytail confirmed only the separate 'both qualify, same org' skip is correct. Reasoned and unverified. The check that would settle it is the repro test above. Note: this is the only Important finding, and both correctness seats raised it independently with a concrete repro. Its exclusion is a product of the agreement threshold, not of its merit, so it should be surfaced to the user.

findings.claim: There is one IdentityProviderListQuery per realm and FetchMode, holding results for every organization ID. Each first-seen org invalidates the shared entry and re-adds a full copy of it (putAll(previous.searchKeys)), which costs O(number of orgs) per miss. The entry grows without bound, and any change to a login-eligible IDP clears the results for all orgs.
findings.evidence: open-code-review cites lines 215 and 232-241. It adds that under concurrent logins for different orgs, each miss bumps the revision and makes other threads' addRevisioned fail, so caching barely works under peak load. superpowers cites lines 233-240. Both contrast this with getByOrganization, which keys per org. Suggested alternative: key by realm + mode + orgId. Reasoned; nothing was run.
findings.reason: Two seats, so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed. Performance concern, reasoned only; a load test with many organizations would settle it.

findings.claim: Javadoc is out of date. The LoginFilter Javadoc (:216) claims the enum lists every field considered for login, but the new org/BROKER_PUBLIC condition is hard-coded in getLoginPredicate(). As a result, getLoginSearchOptions() and getLoginPredicate() no longer encode the same criteria. The getForLogin Javadoc (:151-152) and getFederatedIdentityProviders Javadoc (:202-203) still list only enabled, link-only and hide-on-login.
findings.evidence: mattpocock cites the CONTRIBUTING.md requirement to include relevant documentation. superpowers independently notes the stale Javadoc at 151-152 and 202-203.
findings.reason: Two seats, so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed. It would be subsumed by the documentation fix for the main-list getLoginPredicate finding (line 254).

findings.claim: getForLogin (213-255) duplicates getByOrganization (167-211) almost line for line: the invalid-key bypass, the get/miss/add-search-key branches, the addRevisioned revision choice, and the resolve-by-id loop. The copies have already drifted: getByOrganization bypasses on isInvalid(orgId) and getForLogin does not.
findings.evidence: Side-by-side comparison by ponytail, who calls the drift harmless today. Suggested fix: one private cachedIdpList(cacheKey, searchKey, loader) helper, saving about 35 lines. Reasoned.
findings.reason: One advisory seat, so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed. ponytail: merge getForLogin and getByOrganization into one cachedIdpList helper so future cache fixes land once.

findings.claim: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate (382-418) spends 28 lines, 12 of them restating Javadoc, on one boolean condition. It repeats the FetchMode invalidation loop from registerIDPLoginInvalidation (385-387 vs 415-417) and rebuilds the stream-reduced predicate up to four times per update.
findings.evidence: ponytail reduces the logic to: invalidate iff before != after, or before is true and the org changed. It confirms that the 'both qualify, same org' skip is deliberate, tested (idp-alias-0) and correct. Suggested fix: compute the predicate once per model and share the loop, saving about 15 lines.
findings.reason: One advisory seat, so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed. ponytail: compute before/after once and share the invalidation loop. Any rewrite here should come after the stale-cache finding at line 91, which concerns the same method's inputs.

It does not cover a disabled organization, organization removal, or the isEnabled() re-check added at OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80. There is no browser or login-page level test.

findings.claim: remove() now calls idpDelegate.getByAlias on every remove, even when the cached model is available, adding one database read per remove.
findings.evidence: ponytail calls it 'minor at most' on a rare admin operation. open-code-review checked it and recorded no finding, calling the read negligible and noting that using the raw model is what makes remove() correct.
findings.reason: One seat, so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed. The claim is accurate, but both seats that looked at it judge the impact negligible. open-code-review's correctness argument (the raw model is needed for correct invalidation) argues against removing the read.

coverage: No files skipped: every seat reports reading all 4 patch files (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java, IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java, OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java, OrganizationCacheTest.java). Partial depth: OCR's tool excluded OrganizationCacheTest.java (default_path); the seat read it manually but did not deeply validate its assertions. mattpocock checked the Infinispan provider against documented standards only, not cache correctness. ponytail reviewed only through the over-engineering lens. mattpocock skipped js/CODING_GUIDELINES.md because the patch has no JS. Axes that did not run: (1) Gate: not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored and no finding has ground truth; every finding is reasoned, nothing was built or tested, and the proposed repro test for the line-91 finding was never executed. (2) Spec: no spec was supplied, and issue #32573 was not fetched (the sandbox blocked github.com), so the intent of the getLoginPredicate change is unconfirmed. (3) Cluster invalidation propagation was not checked beyond registerInvalidation sending events (open-code-review, superpowers). (4) Concurrency under real load was not exercised. Merge note: the only Important finding (stale login cache, InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:91) was raised by two correctness seats and so sits in the appendix under the three-seat threshold, while the main list holds only two Minor findings.
